messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Adaptive integration using 'tiny_ad': using pnorm?
parts:
Hi, I have modified (changed dnorm to pnorm) the attached
Adaptive integration example, but it does not compile.

Is there any simple way to fix this, i.e use pnorm() with tiny_ad?

Hans

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Adaptive integration using 'tiny_ad': using pnorm?
parts: Simplest 'fix' would be to use 'pnorm_approx' - that should work for all types as it is based on tanh.

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Adaptive integration using 'tiny_ad': using pnorm?
parts:
To give a more complete answer, it's also easy to expand the derivatives known to tiny_ad. Adding pnorm could be done with:

namespace atomic {
namespace tiny_ad {
  double pnorm(double x) { return Rmath::Rf_pnorm5(x, 0, 1, 1, 0); }
  template<class T, class V>
  ad<T, V> pnorm (const ad<T, V> &x) {
    return dnorm(x, ad<T, V>(0), ad<T, V>(1));
  }
}
}

which would be used as

ans += atomic::tiny_ad::pnorm(u);

On Tuesday, December 5, 2023 at 6:01:41 PM UTC+1 Kasper Kristensen wrote:
Simplest 'fix' would be to use 'pnorm_approx' - that should work for all types as it is based on tanh.
